title: Introduce warmup-decode handshake bridge and kernel negotiator
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Reduced tail latency by ~12% on interactive chat workloads via a warmup-decode handshake and adaptive kernel negotiation. Improves KV cache priming efficiency and stabilizes continuous-batching latency. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: Our current warmup (KV priming) and decode stages operate largely as independent pipelines. Under variable sequence-length traffic and heavy prefix reuse, this causes either wasted KV fetches (overprime) or decode stalls (underprime). This PR introduces a lightweight runtime bridge — the warmup-decode handshake — and a kernel negotiator that together reduce wasted work and smooth decode handoffs.

Summary of changes:
- warmup/handshake: adds a handshake protocol between WarmupService and DecodeScheduler. Warmup emits a lightweight token (warmup_hint) carrying expected KV keys, confidence score, and a preferred kernel slice size. DecodeScheduler consumes hints and decides whether to wait for KV or proceed with speculative decode paths. The handshake supports timed fallbacks to prevent stalls.
- kernel negotiator: runtime component that picks kernel execution parameters (micro-slice size, preferred kernel implementation) based on warmup_hint, sequence-length distribution, and current GPU occupancy. Includes a small reinforcement-like scoring table that biases safer kernels for high-variance inputs.
- probabilistic priming: warmup now emits priming decisions with a configurable probability budget per route to limit wasted KV fetches. The budget decays on successful reuse and replenishes slowly for new contexts.
- queue watermarks & backpressure: Adds per-stage watermarks (low/medium/high) to the continuous-batching queues so the scheduler can choose to batch longer or kick off speculative decodes earlier when queues reach certain levels.
- telemetry & tests: new metrics (warmup.hint_confidence, kernel.negotiator_choice, warmup.priming_efficiency) and unit/integration tests for handshake timing and fallback correctness.

Commits summary:
- 1a2b3c4: initial handshake protocol and warmup_hint protobuf + serialization glue
- 2b3c4d5: kernel negotiator core algorithm and scoring table with unit tests
- 3c4d5e6: probabilistic priming budget implementation + configuration flags
- 4d5e6f7: integrate handshake into DecodeScheduler and add timed fallback path
- 5e6f7g8: add telemetry, dashboards, and e2e canary harness
- 6f7g8h9: address reviewer nits and CI flakes (kv_warmup_test race)

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/warmup/warmup_service.cc - handshake emission, priming budget logic
- runtime/decode/decode_scheduler.cc - handshake consumer, timed fallback, speculative path gating
- runtime/kernel/negotiator.h/.cc - negotiator selection logic + scoring table
- runtime/queues/batch_queue.cc - watermark thresholds, signals to scheduler
- proto/runtime/warmup.proto - warmup_hint definition
- telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml - new metric names
- tests/unit/test_kernel_negotiator.cpp
- tests/integration/test_warmup_handshake.cpp

Benchmark & canary results (internal lab + 10% internal canary):
- Interactive chat workload (mix of short/long tails, median seq=64, p95 seq=512): p95 latency reduced 12% (from 183ms to 161ms) at comparable GPU utilization.
- Throughput: sustained throughput increased ~8% for mixed-seqlen batches due to fewer decode stalls.
- KV priming efficiency: observed ~6 percentage point increase in priming hit-rate on canary traffic after budget tuning (from 74% to 80%).
- CPU/GPU overhead: kernel_negotiator adds ~0.7% CPU usage on the scheduling tower, attributed to scoring table lookups; acceptable within limits.

Backward compatibility: No API changes. Handshake is internal within the runtime; features gated behind runtime flag runtime.experimental.warmup_handshake (default true in canary).

Testing notes and CI history:
- First CI run failed due to a race in kv_warmup_test (intermittent when priming budget thread races with ephemeral eviction). Fixed by adding a small synchronization window and adjusting test timeouts.
- All unit and integration tests now pass on Linux and macOS CI images. Load test harnesses reproduced production-like traffic before canary.

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. Two requests: 1) add a knob to disable probabilistic priming per-route, 2) add more documentation on how the kernel negotiator scoring table is tuned."
- Author (Priya): "Added per-route config and a section in runtime/README.md explaining tuning heuristics and example scoring profiles."
- Maya Patel (reviewer): "Can we ensure that the timed fallback path never increases tail latency under low-load? Add unit test to assert fallback latency bounds."
- Author: "Added targeted integration test and a guard that enforces a max-wait threshold (configurable) to prevent pathological waits."
- Diego Martinez (approver): "Verified canary telemetry and metrics dashboards; approved for merge after CI green."

CI checks: ["unit-tests: passed", "integration-tests: passed", "lint: passed", "bench-lab: passed", "canary-smoke: passed"]

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merge after final CI green and canary verification. Merged by Priya Nair. SHA: abcdef1234567890 (squash).

Notes for operators:

- Dashboards added: warmup/priming_efficiency, warmup/hint_confidence, kernel/negotiator_choice_distribution, decode/handshake_fallback_rate

Follow-ups planned:

- Extend negotiator to incorporate micro-kernel performance models per-GPU family.

If you'd like a staged rollout plan or help interpreting canary telemetry, I can add the Prometheus/Grafana query snippets to the PR notes.
